cards.text: Some time later, King David heads out to war. Friend, this man does NOT believe in the snooze button.

cards.question: Who does David defeat first, taking Metheg-ammah right out of their hand?

cards.text: Next, David defeats the Moabites. He makes them lie down on the ground and measures them off with a cord.

cards.question: Two lengths of David's cord marked the Moabites who would be put to death. One length marked the ones who would be ___.
Now the Moabites are subject to David. What do they start bringing him?

cards.text: Then comes Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, marching out to restore his dominion along a big river. David defeats him, so that's big plans and a SHORT trip.

cards.question: King Hadadezer had marched out to restore his dominion along the ___ River.

cards.text: David captures a thousand chariots, SEVEN thousand charioteers and TWENTY thousand foot soldiers from Hadadezer. Now he's got a whole lot of horses and a decision to make.

cards.question: True or false: David keeps every one of Hadadezer's horses for his own chariots.

cards.text: David hamstrings all the horses except a hundred he keeps for the chariots. Then backup shows up to help King Hadadezer of Zobah.

cards.question: Who comes to help King Hadadezer of Zobah against David?

cards.text: David strikes down twenty-two thousand of their men. That's me diving to save a falling tray of cookies, and now there's a tray on the floor AND a stamper on the floor.

cards.question: David places garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Arameans bring him tribute. Who does the chapter say made David victorious wherever he went?

cards.text: David takes the gold shields that belonged to Hadadezer's officers, plus a large amount of bronze from Betah and Berothai, Hadadezer's cities. I came out of that drawer with ONE gold base, and I thought I was fancy.

cards.question: David brings the gold shields of Hadadezer's officers to ___.

cards.text: Toi, king of Hamath, hears that David defeated Hadadezer's entire army, and Hadadezer had been at war with Toi. I bet Toi read that news twice just to enjoy it.

cards.question: King Toi sends someone to greet King David and bless him for defeating Hadadezer. Who does he send?
Joram brings King David articles of silver and gold and bronze. True or false: David keeps them for his own palace.

cards.text: David dedicates them to the LORD, along with the silver and gold from Edom, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, the Amalekites and Hadadezer's spoil. Me, somebody hands me something shiny and it's going on the counter where EVERYBODY can see it.

cards.question: David returns from striking down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt. What does he make for himself?

cards.text: Then David places garrisons throughout Edom. Friend, this man is putting up garrisons like I put out cooling racks.

cards.question: True or false: Even with David's garrisons in Edom, some of the Edomites stay free of him.

cards.text: All the Edomites are subject to David, and there's that line again about the LORD making David victorious wherever he went. Now David reigns over all Israel.

cards.question: As he reigned over all Israel, David administered ___ and ___ for all his people.

cards.text: Then we meet David's team: Joab son of Zeruiah over the army, plus a recorder, priests, a scribe, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada over the Cherethites and Pelethites, and David's sons are priestly leaders. That's a real org chart, and mine is me, me, and on busy days, also me.

findings.problem: The snooze-button joke is about getting up without delay. The core action of 8:1 is defeating and subduing the Philistines, and the verse opens with 'Some time later,' which points to a gap, not urgency. The comparison doesn't share the action, so it doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'So that's big plans and a SHORT trip' makes Hadadezer the butt of the joke. It laughs at him for losing instead of laughing with a human situation or at Papa Dorin himself.

rule.text: Humble. When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it's himself. Humor about people in Bible stories laughs with their human situation, never at them.

findings.problem: 'Who does the chapter say made David victorious wherever he went?' reads like a test question about the text. It isn't a storyteller pausing inside the moment.

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in. The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.

findings.problem: Nothing before this true/false card hints at what David does with gifts or spoil. The earlier cards only say the gold shields went to Jerusalem. Whether David keeps Joram's silver, gold and bronze or dedicates them is a coin flip, not a reasoned pick.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The card carries three beats: the Edomites subject to David, the repeated line about the LORD making David victorious, and David reigning over all Israel. The first beat also just restates the answer to card 7.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: 'Now David reigns over all Israel' suggests his reign over all Israel starts at this point. Verse 15 says 'Thus David reigned over all Israel,' a summary with no starting time.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The two right answers are tied to fixed blanks, so justice has to go first and righteousness second. Putting them in the other order means the same thing, so the card ends up testing the BSB word order the baker hasn't seen, not the meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The summary of the officials list (8:16-18) goes item by item: Joab over the army, a recorder, priests, a scribe, Benaiah over the Cherethites and Pelethites, and David's sons as priestly leaders. It should say in a few words what the list covers, with at most a standout detail.

rule.text: He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item.
